title: Tuna Salad Sandwich on White Bread with Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: The tuna salad sandwich with cheese on white bread is a sandwich made of a slice of soft white bread topped with a generous layer of tuna salad and melted cheese. It is popular in fast‑food venues and as a quick lunch, combining the mild flavor of fish, creamy cheese, and the soft texture of the bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tuna used in the salad is usually canned in its own juice or oil, making it convenient for fast preparation.
Cream cheese is often added to improve taste and create a smoother texture.
White bread for this sandwich is typically lightly toasted to hold the filling without becoming soggy.
Tuna salad often includes finely chopped onion, celery, mustard or mayonnaise, giving it a distinctive aroma.
The sandwich is commonly served in a hand‑held portion, making it popular in school cafeterias and office cafés.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Tuna contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The tuna salad supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cream cheese adds calcium, contributing to bone and teeth strength.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: The sandwich provides a modest amount of carbs, making it suitable for moderately low‑carb diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with fish allergies.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt, so people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Mercury
items.content: Tuna may accumulate mercury; consumption should be limited, especially for pregnant women and children.

items.title: Lactose in cheese
items.content: Cream cheese contains lactose, which can be problematic for those with lactose intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat with hands, preferably cut in half. It can be served with vegetable sticks, a fresh side salad, or a light dip. For extra freshness, add lettuce, tomato or cucumber slices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. If components are prepared separately, keep tuna salad refrigerated for up to 3 days and cheese for up to 2 weeks. Ensure the bread does not become overly soggy before serving.
